newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open much stronger on payrolls data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open much stronger on payrolls data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened much stronger on Thursday, rallying with U.S. treasuries after the release of a moderate U.S. employment report for June, dealers said.

"The report was viewed as close to expectations but in some aspects maybe a little bit on the weak side, so the bond market in the U.S. is up a point and we've basically kept pace," said Ted Carmichael, head of research with J.P. Morgan Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.09 to C$116.64 to yield 6.703 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose a full point to yield 6.63 percent. The spread between the bonds was seven basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Wednesday.

North American fixed-income markets strengthened this morning after the U.S. Labor Department said payrolls rose by 217,000 in June, while the unemployment rate ticked up to 5.0 percent from 4.8 percent.
A survey of economists had forecast a rise of 222,000 and a steady jobless rate.
In Canada, there has been no major economic data released since Monday.

Trading activity is expected to taper off towards the end of the session in Canada with the U.S. market closing early ahead of the July 1 public and market holiday. However, there has been no announcement of an early close in Canada.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.73 to C$108.32 to yield 6.116 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent which rose 23/32 to yield 6.31 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 19 basis points from 20 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.11 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.15 percent.
